raw_segments.text: Aegius, woman, indeed my heart goes forth to show this help to thee, first for religion's
sake, then for thy promised hope, to heal my ache of childlessness.
Tease this hath made mine whole life as a shadow and starved out my soul, but thus it
Once make thy way to Attic earth, I, as in law I may, will keep thee and befriend.
But in this land, where Creon rules, I may not raise my hand to shelter thee.
Move of thine own essay to seek my house, there thou shall always stay, inviolate,
But come thyself from Corinth, I would fain even in foreign eyes be always just.
